lede: A whole community was thrown into the fire for one offence: believing in Allah. Their killers sat and watched. This surah was sent to believers who were being tortured in Makkah, to tell them who else was watching.

names.name: al-Burūj
names.note: After the oath it opens with, by the sky and its burūj: its great stars, or the stations through which the sun and moon pass. The Prophet ﷺ recited it as Wa-l-samāʾi dhāti l-burūj.

revelation.detail: It is Makkan without disagreement; Ibn al-Jawzī and al-Qurṭubī both record the agreement. The traditional order places it twenty-seventh, in the years when the weaker Muslims of Makkah were being publicly tormented.
revelation.when: The years of persecution in Makkah

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ البُرُوجِ وَهِيَ مَكِّيَّةٌ كُلُّها بِإجْماعِهِمْ
سُورَةُ الْبُرُوجِ مَكِّيَّةٌ بِاتِّفَاقٍ. وَهِيَ ثَنَتَانِ وَعِشْرُونَ آية

attested.quote: أخْرَجَ ابْنُ الضُّرَيْسِ والنَّحّاسُ، وابْنُ مَرْدُويَهَ والبَيْهَقِيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبّاسٍ قالَ: نَزَلَتْ ﴿والسَّماءِ ذاتِ البُرُوجِ﴾ بِمَكَّةَ
attested.says: Ibn ʿAbbās: it came down in Makkah. Recorded by Ibn al-Ḍurays, al-Naḥḥās, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqī.

setting: Bilāl was laid on the burning ground with a rock on his chest. ʿAmmār’s mother, Sumayyah, was killed, and his father died under torture. Khabbāb was pressed onto live coals. The believers of Makkah who had no clan to shield them were being broken one at a time, and they asked the Prophet ﷺ why he did not pray for Allah’s help. He told them of people before them who were sawn in two and combed with iron and did not give up their religion.

This surah gave them such a people. The Prophet ﷺ told the story in full, as Ṣuhayb relates in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim: a king, his sorcerer, and a boy sent to learn sorcery who met a monk on the road and learned faith instead. The king could not kill the boy by any means until the boy told him how: gather the people, and shoot me saying, “In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy.” He did, the boy died — and the people said, “We believe in the Lord of the boy.” So the king had trenches dug and fires lit, and those who would not recant were driven in. A woman came with her infant and hesitated; the child said, “Mother, be patient — you are upon the truth.”

The surah does not say that the believers were rescued. It says that those who burned them are cursed, that the fire of Hell is waiting for anyone who torments believing men and women and does not repent, and that the believers have gardens — “that is the great success.” Victory, in this surah, is to have held on.

occasions.title: The boy, the monk and the king
occasions.text: Ṣuhayb relates that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: there was a king among those who came before you, and he had a sorcerer. When the sorcerer grew old he said to the king: I have grown old; send me a boy to whom I can teach sorcery. A boy was sent. On his road there was a monk, and he sat with him and listened to what he said, and it pleased him. So whenever he went to the sorcerer he would stop and sit with the monk, and the sorcerer would beat him when he arrived. He complained of it to the monk, who said: “When you fear the sorcerer, say: my family kept me. And when you fear your family, say: the sorcerer kept me.”
story: One day he came upon a great beast that had blocked the people’s way. He said: “Today I shall know which is better, the sorcerer or the monk.” He took up a stone and said: “O Allah, if the way of the monk is dearer to You than the way of the sorcerer, kill this beast, so that the people may pass.” He threw it and killed it, and the people went on. He told the monk, who said: “My son, today you are better than I am. You have come to what I see; and you will be tried. If you are tried, do not point to me.”

The boy came to heal the blind and the leper, and to treat people of every ailment. A courtier of the king who had gone blind heard of him and brought him many gifts: “All that is here is yours, if you cure me.” He said: “I cure no one. It is Allah who cures. If you believe in Allah, I will call upon Him and He will heal you.” He believed, and Allah healed him. He went and sat beside the king as he used to, and the king said: “Who gave you back your sight?” — “My Lord.” — “Have you a lord other than me?” — “My Lord and your Lord is Allah.” He was seized and tortured until he pointed to the boy. The boy said the same — “I cure no one; it is Allah who cures” — and was tortured until he pointed to the monk.

The monk was brought and told: give up your religion. He refused; a saw was set on the parting of his head, and he was cut through until his two halves fell. The courtier was told the same, and refused, and it was done to him. Then the boy was told, and refused. The king handed him to some of his men: take him to such-and-such a mountain and climb it with him, and when you reach its summit, if he does not give up his religion, throw him from it. On the mountain he said: “O Allah, deal with them for me however You will.” The mountain shook with them and they fell, and he came walking back to the king. “What became of your companions?” — “Allah dealt with them for me.” He was handed to others, to be taken out in a boat to the middle of the sea and cast overboard. He made the same prayer; the boat capsized and they drowned, and he came walking back to the king.

Then he said to the king: “You will not kill me until you do what I tell you. Gather the people on one open ground and bind me to the trunk of a tree. Then take an arrow from my quiver, set it in the middle of the bow, and say: In the name of Allah, the Lord of the boy. Then shoot me. If you do that, you will kill me.” The king gathered the people and did it. The arrow struck the boy’s temple; he put his hand on the place where it had struck, and died. And the people said: “We believe in the Lord of the boy. We believe in the Lord of the boy. We believe in the Lord of the boy.”

The king was told: do you see? What you feared has come upon you; the people have believed. He ordered trenches to be dug at the openings of the roads, and fires lit in them, and said: whoever does not give up his religion, throw him in. And they did so, until there came a woman with a small child of hers, and she shrank from falling into it. The child said to her: “Mother, be patient. You are upon the truth.”
occasions.source: Ṣuhayb: Muslim (3005), and Aḥmad, as Ibn Kathīr gives it under these ayat.

evidence.quote: عَنْ صُهَيب: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ: "كَانَ مَلِكٌ فِيمَنْ كَانَ قَبْلَكُمْ، وَكَانَ لَهُ سَاحِرٌ، فَلَمَّا كَبُرَ السَّاحِرُ قَالَ لِلْمَلِكِ: إِنِّي قَدْ كَبُرَتْ سِنِّي وَحَضَرَ أَجَلِي

aim: To show Allah’s might and His all-encompassing grasp, and His threat of severe punishment to those who lie in wait for the believers.

outline.title: Three oaths
outline.summary: By the sky with its great stars, by the promised Day, and by a witness and what is witnessed.

outline.title: The makers of the Trench
outline.summary: Cursed were the people of the Trench — of the fire fed with fuel — as they sat beside it, witnesses to what they were doing to the believers. They held nothing against them except that they believed in Allah, the Almighty, the Praiseworthy, to whom belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. And Allah is Witness over all things.

outline.title: The two outcomes
outline.summary: Those who torment believing men and women and then do not repent will have the punishment of Hell, and the punishment of burning. Those who believe and do right will have gardens beneath which rivers flow: that is the great success. Even here, the door of repentance is named.

outline.title: Who He is
outline.summary: The grip of your Lord is severe. It is He who originates and brings back; and He is the Forgiving, the Loving, Lord of the Throne, the Glorious, Doer of whatever He wills.

outline.title: The armies before
outline.summary: Has the story of the hosts reached you — Pharaoh and Thamūd? Yet the disbelievers persist in denial, while Allah surrounds them from behind. This is a glorious Qurʾan, in a Preserved Tablet.

keyAyah.why: The charge against the believers, stated exactly. It has been the charge in every age since.

virtues.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to recite, in the noon and afternoon prayers, “By the sky with its great stars” and “By the sky and the night-comer”, and surahs like them.

before: Al-Inshiqāq ended with an unfailing reward for those who believe and do right. Al-Burūj shows what believing cost some of them, and calls their end the great success.
after: Al-Burūj swears by the sky and its stars; al-Ṭāriq by the sky and one star. There the watching was Allah’s over a people; here it is over each soul.

notable.label: Those who torment the believers and do not repent
A glorious Qurʾan, in a Preserved Tablet

sources: Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim; the Sunan of Abū Dāwūd and al-Tirmidhī
